transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-28 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE); Marcus Flynn (Redwood SE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Raj Patel (NimbleWare CTO); Anna Gomez (Lead ML Engineer); Tom Wu (SRE); Meera Singh (Product)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on routing (when to route to cheaper model / fallback) and hosting mode rubric (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Agreed on acceptance criteria to be a combination of p95 latency, cost per 1k requests, and accuracy regression threshold vs baseline. Decided to run a 2-phase benchmark: synthetic concurrency sweep + representative traffic replay. Timeline: 3-week technical sprint for benchmarks + 1 week to decide contract.

Topics:
- Success criteria and acceptance thresholds
- Workload sizing and burn-rate estimates
- Benchmark plan and who runs which tests
- Hosting mode tradeoffs (latency/cost/security)
- Timeline and decision gates

Action items (recap at top): Marcus to send runbook; Anna to send sample queries; Lena to share pricing & Dedicated sizing; Tom to provide infra constraints/KMS info.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for carving time, quick roll call, and then we'll jump in. we want to make sure the POC gives you a deterministic decision between hosted, dedicated, and private.
[00:18] Raj (NimbleWare): yep, thanks Lena, excited. quick context — we're moving from a batch extract system to real-time assistant on our platform, target is 200 qps peak for inference and p95 under, uh, 120 to 150 ms ideally.
[00:31] Marcus (Redwood): got it, thanks. just to set expectations: we usually split POC into two phases — throughput/latency bench with synthetic load, then a replay of your representative traffic to check quality and cost. sound good?
[00:44] Raj: yeah, that matches what we think. one thing — security is non-negotiable for us. SOC2 type 2, SSO, KMS for keys, and we need audit logs accessible for 12 months. is that all supported?
[00:58] Lena: short answer yes, all supported. hosted has SOC2 and KMS integrations, Dedicated gives you isolated pools and custom routing, Private (VPC/on-prem) gives control over keys and network but has longer setup. Marcus will call out what is different during the benchmarks.
[01:15] Anna (NimbleWare): can we talk error budgets? like if we target p95 120 ms, what does graceful degradation look like — fall back to smaller model? route to hosted vs dedicated?
[01:28] Marcus: good question. our routing model is policy-driven — you can set latency SLOs, cost caps, and model-variant fallbacks. for example if p95 breaches on Dedicated we can route to a cheaper hosted model variant or allow slight increase for a short window. tradeoffs are obvious: routing off Dedicated to hosted adds egress and possibly more latency depending on region.
[01:51] Tom (NimbleWare SRE): region question: our data plane sits in eu-west-1, and some users are in ap-south, so multi-region routing matters. Dedicated in same region is preferable for latency. hosted region availability — do you have eu-west infra for the specific models we plan to use?
[02:06] Marcus: yes, we have hosted capacity in eu-west and us-west, model availability varies, we'll list exact models. Dedicated pools you reserve in region. Private on-prem obviously is local but needs infra ops.
[02:18] Meera (Product): success criteria — can we summarize? accuracy not worse than 1.5% relative to baseline; p95 under 120 ms for 95% of requests; cost less than $X per 10k requests (TBD). also run warm/cold cache tests.
[02:33] Lena: sounds reasonable. we'll put concrete numbers in the runbook; we usually want both quality/accuracy checks over a labeled subset plus latency/throughput sweeps.
[02:40] Raj: about cost — we are sensitive. hosted looks easiest but worried monthly burn will be high. Dedicated maybe best for predictable traffic, but commitment and scaling levers?
[02:50] Marcus: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput per GPU pool, autoscale on top is available but with longer spin-up times. Dedicated tends to be 30-60% cheaper per token at scale depending on quantization and model. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but at higher unit cost, and Private has higher fixed ops cost but best for data residency and strict KMS control.
[03:10] Anna: can we do hybrid? start hosted for quick launch and then move critical paths to Dedicated?
[03:16] Lena: absolutely; that's a common path — we call it onramp: hosted for early traffic, Dedicated for steady high-volume routes, Private for regulated workloads. routing policy decides which request goes where.
[03:27] Raj: what about KV cache / prefix caching? That's critical for us because many queries share prefixes.
[03:33] Marcus: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and will keep hot keys in memory. for Dedicated there's more control on cache TTL and memory allocation; hosted has optimistic caching and we can expose hit rates in Console.
[03:50] Tom: any differences in monitoring & tracing? we need correlation ids and full traces into our datadog.
[03:57] Diego (Redwood): we have tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdowns via the Console and an API; Dedicated & Private can push logs to your SIEM, hosted has integrations as well but with more managed retention policies.
[04:12] Anna: ok perfect. let's get into benchmark specifics — Marcus, what do you need from our side?
[04:16] Marcus: for the replay phase we need: sample queries (50–5k rows, anonymized), distribution of sequence lengths, expected tokens per response, concurrency profile (baseline, peak), and any path with multi-turn chat to test kv-cache. also, identify any disallowed PII patterns so we can mask.
[04:36] Anna: we can share a 4k sample of production queries, and sequence lengths. we need to scrub PII — will do that by Friday.
[04:44] Marcus: great. for the synthetic sweep we will run a QPS ramp from 1 qps to 300 qps in steps, measure p50, p95, errors, and memory utilization on the host. we'll run that on Hosted and Dedicated config to compare.
[04:58] Raj: 300 qps is high — our peak is 200 but with bursts; can you simulate bursty traffic?
[05:04] Marcus: yes, we'll do step and spike patterns and see tail latency.
[05:09] Meera: timeline? you mentioned two phases — how long to run each?
[05:12] Lena: typical is 1 week to configure and run synthetic bench, 1 week to run replay and analysis, then 1 week buffer for follow-ups — so ~3 weeks. given approvals and infra we can compress to 2 if customer prioritizes.
[05:26] Tom: what's the expected instrumentation effort on our side? i.e. do we need to install anything?
[05:30] Marcus: minimal — for hosted we give you API keys and tracing headers, for Dedicated/Private we'll ask for a small agent to run for metrics scraping if you want Prometheus exports; otherwise we can provide hosted metrics.
[05:44] Anna: what about model selection — we plan to use an open LLM ~13B for generation and a smaller 3B for reranking. recommendations?
[05:51] Marcus: good combo. for latency-sensitive endpoints you can use the 3B or quantized 13B. we'll include quantization profiles in the runbook. Dedicated tends to allow int8 that helps cost.
[06:03] Raj: benchmark acceptance — how do we decide pass/fail?
[06:07] Lena: pass/fail will be a checklist: p95 latency threshold (e.g., <120ms), accuracy delta <1.5% on test set, error rate <0.5%, and cost estimate within target burn. we'll draft the checklist and you'll confirm.
[06:22] Anna: can you also capture cold-start behavior? some of our pods scale up from zero.
[06:27] Marcus: yes synthetic will include cold-starts and warm runs; we'll log first-token latencies and per-connection overhead.
[06:35] Tom: for Private deployment — we need an estimate for ops effort. how long to stand up on-prem?
[06:41] Diego: on-prem timeline is variable — if you have infra ready, air-gapped install takes 6–8 weeks with our packaging; VPC/private cloud with MDM can be 3–6 weeks. longer than hosted/dedicated which are near immediate.
[06:55] Raj: ok that's a factor. one more: data residency. we must keep EU customer data in EU. hosted seems to have eu-west but need proof.
[07:03] Lena: we'll provide the region list and SOC2 artifacts; for Dedicated you can choose region; Private you control everything.
[07:10] Meera: what about fallback strategies — routing cost-sensitive traffic to a smaller model automatically? will that affect quality metrics?
[07:17] Marcus: routing rules can fall back to cheaper model variants with a configurable quality delta; we'll measure impact in the replay phase and surface quality signals per request. you can opt-in per-route.
[07:32] Raj: any gotchas we should know — egress, network, or throttling?
[07:36] Marcus: egress charges apply if data leaves region, also if routing to hosted from Dedicated you'll see egress and extra latency. throttling only occurs when your pool limits are reached; autoscale rules can be tuned.
[07:48] Anna: how do you handle secret management and KMS? we use HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS.
[07:54] Diego: we integrate with customer KMS via API; Dedicated/Private can use your KMS directly, hosted uses a managed KMS but supports customer-managed keys in certain plans. we'll map this in the security doc.
[08:08] Raj: what's a realistic cost delta — rough numbers suffice now — between hosted, dedicated, private for 1M requests / month?
[08:16] Marcus: rough, back-of-envelope: hosted could be $0.XX per 1k tokens, Dedicated typically 30–60% cheaper at scale, Private is cheaper per token maybe 50% off hosted but with infra/ops overhead; we'll put concrete in the pricing doc once we have your traffic profile and model choices.
[08:31] Meera: ok. one last thing — decision gates. we want a rubric to decide after the POC: performance, cost, security, ops. can you propose a weighted scoring?
[08:40] Lena: yes, we can draft a rubric: Performance (40%), Cost (30%), Security/Compliance (20%), Ops Complexity (10%). we can tweak weights based on your priorities.
[08:51] Raj: that helps. can we get a template?
[08:54] Lena: yes Marcus will include a scoring template in the runbook.
[09:00] [wrap up recap]
[09:02] Lena: recap — Marcus shares runbook + scoring template; Anna sends sample queries; Tom shares infra/KMS constraints; Lena shares dedicated sizing + pricing; schedule benchmark kickoff once artifacts are in.
[09:12] Raj: thanks all, we'll prioritize and get you the samples this week.
[09:16] Lena: great, thanks everyone.

End transcript.
